title: Vincent de Paul (1581–1660)
hookLine: a priest who organized charity across France
tomorrow: Louise de Marillac and the Daughters of Charity

cards: Sunday morning in a small country parish. Just before Mass, someone tells the new priest about a family in a farmhouse outside town: everyone in it is sick, and nobody is looking after them.
He mentions them in his sermon. That afternoon, it seems the whole parish walks out along the road with bread, soup and wine. It's beautiful.
It's also chaos. Too much is arriving on one day, more than the family can use before it spoils, and next week they'll be alone again. The priest watches and thinks: love needs a plan.
His name is Vincent de Paul.

teach.h: A YOUNG PRIEST WHO WANTED COMFORT.
teach.b: First, the young Vincent. Tradition, and Vincent's own later words, suggest that as a young priest he wanted a comfortable post and a good income. He found work in a rich household as tutor and chaplain, close to power.
Through that household he met the poor of the countryside: peasants dying with no one to hear their confession, parishes without real priests.

He began preaching missions in the villages, and gathered priests to do it with him. They became the Congregation of the Mission, and their motto came from Luke's Gospel, where Jesus reads from Isaiah.
In the Douay-Rheims: "he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor." Third, the plan.

After the whole parish showed up at the sick family's door, Vincent gathered the women of the town and wrote a simple rule: who goes on which day, what they bring, how they speak to the sick, how the money is kept.
That small group, a Confraternity of Charity, became a model he spread to parish after parish. Fourth, the reach.
He was chaplain to convicts chained to the oars of the king's galleys. He raised money from the wealthy for the hungry in war-torn regions.

teach.h: TO PREACH THE GOSPEL TO THE POOR.
teach.b: He worked with rich ladies and poor country girls alike. His gift wasn't only compassion; it was the clipboard. Charity done once, in a rush, he believed, can leave people worse off.
Charity with a schedule, a budget and a rule can last.

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Vincent de Paul, and parish groups of the Society of Saint Vincent de Paul, named for him, visit people in need at home, run food pantries and thrift stores, and keep simple rules about how they serve.

o: a men's fraternity house at a Catholic college
a parish group bound by a rule of charity
a council of priests that advises the bishop

games.q: Vincent de Paul — tap the pairs.
p: too much food on one day

s: Vincent wanted to serve the poor from the start
as a young priest he seems to have wanted comfort and a good income. the poor turned him around.
when the whole parish helped at once, the family got more than it could use
too much on one day, then nothing after. that's what convinced him that love needs a plan.
Vincent worked only with the poor
he worked with rich ladies and the powerful too, raising money for the hungry.

games.q: you're Vincent. the whole parish rushed out to feed a sick family, with more food than it can use before it spoils. what do you do next?
o: tell people to stop helping on their own.
gather volunteers and write a simple rule for who goes when.
games.why: he wrote a rule and formed a Confraternity of Charity, then spread the model to parish after parish.

practice: Think of a need near you that keeps coming back, a neighbor who needs rides, a friend who's grieving, a shelter that runs short at month's end, and instead of one big gesture, picture a small plan: who could share it, which day, what exactly you'd bring.
Let the plan get boring and specific; that's the point. If you pray, offer it to God; if not, simply let it take shape.

wordCard.voice: Confraternity. The group of women Vincent de Paul gathered in a parish with a simple rule for visiting the sick, a model he spread from town to town.

orig.note: Latin: 'he sent me to preach the gospel to the poor', from Luke 4:18 in the Vulgate, the motto of Vincent's Congregation of the Mission.

carryVoice: Your line: charity, organized. Love on a schedule outlasts love in a rush. Until tomorrow.
